dialect.detail: RM/COBOL dialect — SOURCE-COMPUTER and OBJECT-COMPUTER both set to RMCOBOL; uses RM/COBOL screen-handling extensions (DISPLAY ... LINE ... POSITION ... CONTROL, ACCEPT ... ESCAPE KEY, WINDOW-CREATE/WINDOW-REMOVE controls)

purpose.domain_detail: Turkish-language general-purpose lookup/selection popup window — likely part of a larger business application (Turkish variable names: DTIP, DTIP-ADI, DTIP-NO suggest a 'type' or category lookup table)
purpose.summary: TIPSEC is a subprogram that implements a scrollable popup list-selection window. It accepts window coordinates and a key, opens a keyed file (DTIP), displays records in a bordered window with box-drawing characters, and allows the user to navigate (arrow keys, PgUp/PgDn, Home, End, Ctrl-Home, Ctrl-End) and select a record, returning the selected code and name to the caller via LINKAGE SECTION parameters.

notable_features: LINKAGE SECTION with USING clause — called subprogram
RM/COBOL screen extensions: DISPLAY LINE/POSITION/CONTROL with BCOLOR/FCOLOR
Box-drawing characters for window border (É, Í, », È, ¼, º)
ACCEPT FROM ESCAPE KEY for function-key handling
Keyed sequential file navigation (START, READ NEXT, READ PREVIOUS)
COPY directives for file-control, FD, status, and window copybooks
No COMP-3, no SQL, no CICS
verdict.notes: File decoded with latin-1 which is consistent with Turkish box-drawing and special characters. The program is clearly part of a larger Turkish RM/COBOL business application. Variable names and logic are in Turkish (e.g., SATIR=row, EKRAN=screen, BILGI=info, YUKARI=up, ASAGI=down). The GOTO usage is present despite COBOL-85 structured constructs also being used.
